source: credit-risk-sql pipeline (./run.sh, default 40,000 loans, seed 42) run on a scratch copy; the raw data is SYNTHETIC, generated by scripts/generate_data.py to mimic Lending Club's structure and messiness

steps.step: Load raw CSVs into all-TEXT staging tables
Deduplicate loans with ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY loan_id)
Deduplicate borrowers with ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY borrower_id)
Impute blank incomes with the SQL-computed median
Normalise home_ownership casing, bucket rare values to OTHER
Cast messy strings: rate '13.5 %' -> 13.5, term ' 36 months' -> 36, 3 date formats -> year
steps.detail: 31,034 raw rate strings carried a % sign; 0 rows failed to parse

steps.step: Engineer target is_default from free-text loan_status
Join loans to borrowers, drop open loans, add income band
steps.detail: 7,308 open loans excluded; overall default rate 19.3%

sample.note: The same 8 loans before (staging, all text) and after (typed) cleaning; raw columns show the borrower's raw fields joined in

raw.issue: duplicate row (same loan_id appears twice) + space-padded ' 7.9% ' rate + blank home_ownership -> OTHER
blank income -> median imputed in SQL
income outlier -> capped at the 99th percentile
missing grade -> NULL (kept, excluded from grade view)
still-open loan -> no outcome, excluded from analysis; 'Mon YYYY' date
lower-case 'rent' -> RENT, ' 60 months' term, '6.06 %' rate, blank income
rare 'ANY' ownership -> OTHER; Charged Off -> default=1; 'YYYY-MM' date
'10+ years' -> 10; Late (31-120 days) -> default=1; bare-number rate

sqlSteps.caption: Median income computed in SQL (SQLite has no MEDIAN): take the middle row(s) of the ordered non-nulls.
sqlSteps.sql:
WITH incomes AS (
    SELECT CAST(annual_inc AS REAL) AS inc
    FROM stg_borrowers
    WHERE annual_inc IS NOT NULL AND TRIM(annual_inc) <> ''
),
ranked AS (
    SELECT inc,
           ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY inc) AS rn,
           COUNT(*)     OVER ()             AS n
    FROM incomes
),
median_inc AS (
    SELECT AVG(inc) AS m FROM ranked WHERE rn IN ((n + 1) / 2, (n + 2) / 2)
),

sqlSteps.caption: 99th-percentile income, used as the outlier cap.
sqlSteps.sql:
p99_inc AS (
    SELECT inc AS cap
    FROM ranked
    WHERE rn = CAST(0.99 * n AS INTEGER)
    LIMIT 1
),

sqlSteps.caption: Deduplicate borrowers: keep one row per borrower_id with ROW_NUMBER().
sqlSteps.sql:
dedup AS (
    SELECT *,
           ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY borrower_id ORDER BY borrower_id) AS rn
    FROM stg_borrowers
    WHERE borrower_id IS NOT NULL AND TRIM(borrower_id) <> ''
)

sqlSteps.caption: Income: cast, impute the median when blank, cap at p99.
sqlSteps.sql:
-- income: cast -> impute median if null -> cap at p99
    MIN(
        COALESCE(
            NULLIF(TRIM(d.annual_inc), '') + 0.0,
            (SELECT m FROM median_inc)
        ),
        (SELECT cap FROM p99_inc)
    ),

sqlSteps.caption: home_ownership: upper-case and bucket rare/blank values into OTHER.
sqlSteps.sql:
CASE UPPER(TRIM(COALESCE(d.home_ownership, '')))
        WHEN 'RENT'     THEN 'RENT'
        WHEN 'MORTGAGE' THEN 'MORTGAGE'
        WHEN 'OWN'      THEN 'OWN'
        ELSE 'OTHER'
    END,

sqlSteps.caption: Deduplicate loans: exact duplicate rows share a loan_id; keep the first.
sqlSteps.sql:
WITH dedup AS (
    -- exact duplicate loan rows share a loan_id; keep the first occurrence
    SELECT *,
           ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY loan_id ORDER BY loan_id) AS rn
    FROM stg_loans
    WHERE loan_id IS NOT NULL AND TRIM(loan_id) <> ''
)

sqlSteps.caption: Term ' 36 months' / '60' -> integer months; rate ' 13.5% ' -> 13.5.
sqlSteps.sql:
-- term " 36 months" / "60" -> integer months
    CASE
        WHEN d.term LIKE '%60%' THEN 60
        WHEN d.term LIKE '%36%' THEN 36
        ELSE NULL
    END,
    -- int_rate " 13.5% " -> 13.5  (strip % and whitespace, then cast)
    CAST(REPLACE(REPLACE(TRIM(d.int_rate), '%', ''), ' ', '') AS REAL),

sqlSteps.caption: Issue date in three formats ('Dec-2018', '2018-12', 'Dec 2018') -> year.
sqlSteps.sql:
-- issue_d in mixed formats ('Dec-2018', '2018-12', 'Dec 2018') -> year
    CASE
        WHEN d.issue_d GLOB '[0-9][0-9][0-9][0-9]-*' THEN CAST(SUBSTR(d.issue_d, 1, 4) AS INTEGER)
        ELSE CAST(SUBSTR(TRIM(d.issue_d), -4) AS INTEGER)
    END,

sqlSteps.caption: Target: Fully Paid -> 0, any delinquency -> 1, still open -> NULL.
sqlSteps.sql:
-- TARGET: Fully Paid -> 0, any delinquency -> 1, still-open -> NULL (excluded)
    CASE
        WHEN d.loan_status = 'Fully Paid'                                 THEN 0
        WHEN d.loan_status IN ('Charged Off', 'Default', 'Late (31-120 days)') THEN 1
        ELSE NULL
    END

sqlSteps.caption: Join loans to borrowers, keep only known outcomes, bucket income.
sqlSteps.sql:
CREATE TABLE analysis_loans AS
SELECT
    l.loan_id,
    l.grade,
    l.purpose,
    l.term_months,
    l.int_rate,
    l.loan_amnt,
    l.issue_year,
    l.is_default,
    b.home_ownership,
    b.addr_state,
    b.annual_inc,
    b.dti,
    CASE
        WHEN b.annual_inc <  40000 THEN '1. <40k'
        WHEN b.annual_inc <  70000 THEN '2. 40-70k'
        WHEN b.annual_inc < 100000 THEN '3. 70-100k'
        WHEN b.annual_inc < 150000 THEN '4. 100-150k'
        ELSE '5. 150k+'
    END AS income_band
FROM clean_loans l
JOIN clean_borrowers b ON b.borrower_id = l.borrower_id
WHERE l.is_default IS NOT NULL;      -- only loans with a known outcome

sqlSteps.caption: Default rate by grade.
sqlSteps.sql:
CREATE VIEW v_default_by_grade AS
SELECT grade,
       COUNT(*)                         AS loans,
       SUM(is_default)                  AS defaults,
       ROUND(100.0 * AVG(is_default), 2) AS default_rate_pct,
       ROUND(AVG(int_rate), 2)          AS avg_int_rate
FROM analysis_loans
WHERE grade IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY grade
ORDER BY grade;

caveats: Synthetic data: the default-rate patterns are planted by the generator (GRADE_DEFAULT_P x PURPOSE_RISK, x1.15 for 60-month), so the analysis recovers them rather than discovering them.

Generator fixes (2026-11-20): each term now gets only its own spellings, so 36- and 60-month loans are labelled correctly; data-entry income outliers are now 0.3% of borrowers, so the 99th-percentile cap lands in the real income distribution.
